_readme: Byte-locks for the consent-marker vocabulary shared by book-consent-spans.ts and audit-consent-signoff.ts (PR #15619). TEXT ONLY, hex-in-JSON, per .claude/rules/no-binary-in-proof-lineage.md — every byte-lock here is diffable in a git diff. Regenerate deliberately, never to make a test pass: a changed hash means the canonical form changed, which means every consent already given against the old form is now stale.
canonicalization: trailing spaces and tabs stripped per line
leading and trailing blank lines stripped

vectors.name: consent-signoff-design-section-4-example
vectors.why: The EXACT example printed in CONSENT-SIGNOFF-DESIGN.md section 4. It is the one vector both implementations can derive independently from published text, so it is the cross-implementation anchor.

vectors.name: crlf-and-trailing-whitespace-are-noise
vectors.why: Canonicalization is deliberately minimal: CRLF -> LF, trailing whitespace per line, surrounding blank lines. Nothing else. If a fifth normalization is ever added, this vector breaks and the addition has to be argued for.

vectors.name: one-character-edit-changes-the-hash
vectors.why: Same passage as above with a single comma added. Consent binds to TEXT: a one-character edit must produce a different sha256 or the staleness detection is theatre.

vectors.name: fenced-example-is-not-an-assertion
vectors.why: A marker inside a code fence must produce NO span. Without this the design docs would register live consent spans about real people.

vectors.name: deidentified-mode-is-carried
vectors.why: mode=deidentified is first-class and travels with the span; the index shows it and #15619 gates on it.

footprintFold.why: footprintOf folds the ordered (spanId, sha256) pairs, ordinal by spanId, into one value. This is what consent binds to when a person consents to their WHOLE portrayal rather than to one passage.

orderIsOrdinalNotInsertion.why: the same two members supplied in the other order must fold to the SAME value, or the hash is machine-dependent
